subject: How to adjust the entire theme "text sizing"?

messages.author: 94d13e337c7d7a78
messages.subject: How to adjust the entire theme "text sizing"?
parts:
All,

I am hoping there is an easy solution: in plot, lattice graphics,
and now ggplot2, I find myself writing LOTS of lines of code just to
fix the text sizing. Maybe I am getting old too quickly, but the text
on EVERYTHING is too small.
Is there a simple line in ggplot2 that I could write that looks
something like:

opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15))

but that works for ALL text? Maybe something like

opts(text=theme_text(size=15))

?

I know that specific example doesn't work, but hopefully something
equally easy. Maybe something that works like how cex() works for the
regular "plot" function.

I would like a command that can scale the text in a relative
sense, leaving the plot title slightly larger than the sub-titles,
etc. Even better would be if there were 2 methods: (a) one that
could expand the entire set of text, so that everything gets "twice as
big", for instance, and (b) one that could expand or shrink the
relative difference between text so that I could, for instance, make
the difference between the largest text & the smallest text change
from 10% to 50% to whatever.
With just these 2 commands, I could adjust the text size to
anything I'd be happy with.

Thanks!
Mike Williamson
